<section class="proj-q" aria-labelledby="h-question">
<h2 id="h-question"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Research question</h2>
<p class="proj-question">What would it take for small modular reactors to power data centers, and which economic dimensions must a credible techno-economic assessment capture?</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-insight" id="insight" aria-labelledby="h-insight">
<h2 id="h-insight"><i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key insight</h2>
<p class="insight-title">Reliability requirements add a capital premium that levelized cost leaves out</p>
<p>A hyperscale campus needs Tier IV-level availability, so one reactor is not enough: with N+1 redundancy, a 300 MW campus may need 400 MW of SMR capacity. Standard levelized-cost estimates omit this reliability premium, so they understate the cost of firm on-site supply.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-contribution">
<h2 id="h-contribution"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>My contribution</h2>
<p>Co-first author. Wrote the techno-economic analysis section, introduction and conclusions.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" id="approach" aria-labelledby="h-approach">
<h2 id="h-approach"><i class="bi bi-tools" aria-hidden="true"></i>How I approached it</h2>
<ol class="approach">
<li class="ap-card"><p class="ap-challenge"><span class="ap-k">Challenge</span>Published SMR cost figures mix first-of-a-kind budgets with long-run nth-of-a-kind targets.</p><p class="ap-did"><span class="ap-k">What I did</span>I set first-of-a-kind and nth-of-a-kind capital costs of SMR projects side by side and argued that assessments treat them as separate cases, each with its own financing and risk.</p><p class="ap-why"><span class="ap-k">Why it mattered</span>Long-run figures make first projects look more viable than they are, and early data-center buyers carry that risk.</p></li>
<li class="ap-card"><p class="ap-challenge"><span class="ap-k">Challenge</span>Levelized cost of electricity leaves out cooling, which takes 30–40% of a hyperscale facility&#x27;s energy.</p><p class="ap-did"><span class="ap-k">What I did</span>In the section I drafted, I proposed a service-based metric, the levelized cost of computing, which puts electricity and cooling costs over units of computing service.</p><p class="ap-why"><span class="ap-k">Why it mattered</span>It compares on-site nuclear, grid and renewable-plus-storage supply by what each delivers to the data center.</p></li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-method">
<h2 id="h-method"><i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Method</h2>
<p>Perspective synthesizing technology, economics and policy for SMR-powered data centers.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-findings">
<h2 id="h-findings"><i class="bi bi-lightbulb" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key findings</h2>
<ol class="findings">
<li>Data-center reliability requirements add a substantial premium to the capital cost of on-site nuclear supply.</li>
<li>First-of-a-kind and nth-of-a-kind cost estimates for SMRs diverge widely, so assumptions must be explicit.</li>
<li>Service-based metrics, such as cost per unit of computing, and co-products such as heat matter for comparisons.</li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec proj-bounds" aria-labelledby="h-bounds">
<h2 id="h-bounds"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Boundary conditions</h2>
<p>A Perspective: it frames the questions and evidence rather than presenting a new case-study model.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-next" id="led-to" aria-labelledby="h-next">
<h2 id="h-next"><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>What it led to</h2>
<p>Pricing the heat used for cooling, hour by hour, became the core of my boundary analysis for one data-center campus. <a class="next-link" href="nuclear-dc.html">Small modular reactor cogeneration for a hyperscale data center<i class="bi bi-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></a></p>
</section>
